name: Cooled tubular reactor: phthalic anhydride
description: One tube of a multitubular reactor oxidizing o-xylene (1 mol% in air) to phthalic anhydride on a vanadium catalyst, cooled along its length by a molten-salt bath in countercurrent. The textbook case for a hot spot (Froment and Bischoff, Chemical Reactor Analysis and Design): the pseudo-homogeneous rate r = k p(xylene) p(O2), ln k = 19.837 - 13636/T in kmol/(kg cat h atm²), is converted to mol/(m³ s Pa²) with a bed density of 1300 kg/m³. The heat of reaction comes from the formation enthalpies (1.12 MJ/mol, less than the 1.29 MJ/mol of the book's lumped scheme), so the hot spot is milder than there. The reactor results give the hot-spot temperature and position; its profiles show both sides of the wall. Raise the salt temperature a few kelvin to see how sensitive the hot spot is.
